mainTopic: How many judges each kind of case needs, from three up to seventy-one, and the פסוקים behind the court sizes
overview: The opening משנה of מסכת סנהדרין lists how many judges are needed for each kind of case. Money cases, damages and fines need three judges, with disputes about מוציא שם רע and מכות, where some say twenty-three. Calendar decisions, court ceremonies like עריפת עגלה and חליצה, and appraisals of holy items also need three, but land and people need nine plus a כהן. Capital cases need twenty-three, and this includes animals that are put to death. Some matters need the great court of seventy-one: trying a שבט, a נביא השקר or a כהן גדול, going to a מלחמת הרשות, expanding ירושלים, setting up local courts, and declaring an עיר הנדחת. The משנה then proves the sizes of the courts from פסוקים: seventy elders plus משה make seventy-one, and two groups of ten make twenty. It begins to explain the last three judges with the rule that convicting needs a majority of two, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Money and damage cases need three judges
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that דיני ממונות, robbery, injury, damages, half-damage, double payment and four-or-five payment are all judged by three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Money cases are judged by three judges. Robbery and injury cases are judged by three. Full damage, half damage, double payment, and four-or-five payment cases are judged by three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת by listing different kinds of money cases and saying each one needs a court of three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list moves from ordinary money disputes to cases that are more like penalties, such as כפל and ארבעה וחמשה. The משנה stresses that even these penalty payments still only need three judges. It repeats "בשלשה" after each group to make this clear.

keyTerms.meaning: Monetary cases, such as loans and money disputes
Robbery and personal injury
Half-damage, paid when an ox with no history of goring gores
Double payment by a thief
Four or five times payment by a thief who slaughtered or sold a stolen sheep or ox

phrases.english: MISHNA: Monetary cases are judged by three judges.
Robbery and injury cases are judged by three.
Full damage and half damage,
double payment
and four-or-five payment are judged by three.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: All monetary and damage cases, including penalty payments like כפל and ארבעה וחמשה, are judged by a court of three.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: rape, seduction and defamation cases need three
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that cases of אונס, מפתה and מוציא שם רע are also judged by three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rapist, a seducer, and one who spreads a bad name are judged by three. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds three more cases that carry a fixed fine, and רבי מאיר says they are also judged by three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases have set payments written in the תורה, and to רבי מאיר they are basically money cases, so three judges are enough. Naming רבי מאיר tells us this is not agreed on. The next step brings the חכמים who argue about מוציא שם רע.

keyTerms.meaning: One who rapes a young unmarried girl and must pay a fine
One who seduces a young unmarried girl and must pay a fine
A husband who falsely claims his new wife was unfaithful during אירוסין

phrases.english: The rapist and the seducer
and the one who spreads a bad name are judged by three.
phrases.notes: This is the husband who falsely claims his bride was unfaithful (דברים 22:13–19).

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹנֵס וְהַמְפַתֶּה וְהַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע – בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list of three-judge cases to fines, now in the name of one תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, אונס, מפתה and מוציא שם רע are all judged by three.

steps.title: The חכמים: a defamation case needs twenty-three
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that מוציא שם רע needs a court of twenty-three, because it involves דיני נפשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: one who spreads a bad name is judged by twenty-three, because it includes a capital case.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר about one case only, מוציא שם רע. They say it needs twenty-three judges, the size of a court for capital cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's claim can lead to a death penalty, either for the wife if the witnesses are believed or for the witnesses if they are found to be עדים זוממין. So the case is not only about money, and it needs a court that can judge life-and-death cases. The חכמים do not argue about אונס and מפתה, which stay at three.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-three, the size of a court that judges capital cases (סנהדרי קטנה)
Capital cases, cases that can end in a death penalty

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים only argue about מוציא שם רע. They agree with רבי מאיר that אונס and מפתה need only three.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a major theme of the מסכת: the size of the court depends on what could happen in the case, not just on what is being claimed.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
one who spreads a bad name is judged by twenty-three,
because it includes a capital case.
phrases.notes: If the claim is proven, the wife could be put to death. If the witnesses are proven false, they could be.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע – בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי מאיר's ruling, but only for מוציא שם רע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, מוציא שם רע is judged by twenty-three because it can become a capital case.

steps.title: Lashes: three judges, or twenty-three according to רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that מכות are judged by three. In רבי ישמעאל's name it was said they need twenty-three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lashes are judged by three. In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said: by twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to cases where someone may get lashes. It gives one opinion of three judges and a second, from רבי ישמעאל, of twenty-three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the punishment is physical, not money, so it is a new kind of case. The first opinion still treats it as a three-judge case. רבי ישמעאל's opinion treats lashes as serious enough to need a larger court. The משנה does not give his reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes given by בית דין for breaking certain prohibitions
In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: Money cases, damages and fines need three judges. The disputes are about cases that come close to physical punishment: מוציא שם רע, where the חכמים say twenty-three, and מכות, where רבי ישמעאל says twenty-three.

phrases.english: Lashes are judged by three.
In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said:
by twenty-three.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַכּוֹת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה. מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמְרוּ: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from money and fine cases to physical punishment by lashes, with a new dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, מכות are judged by three. According to רבי ישמעאל, they are judged by twenty-three.

steps.title: Adding a day to the month or a month to the year needs three judges
steps.stepSummary: עיבור החדש is done by three. According to רבי מאיר, עיבור השנה is also done by three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Making a month 'full' (30 days) is done by three judges. Making a year a leap year is also done by three judges. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from money and punishment cases to calendar decisions. It says both עיבור החדש and עיבור השנה are decided by three judges, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new kind of case: no one is suing anyone, but the court still has to decide. רבי מאיר treats even the big decision of adding a month to the year as a regular three-judge matter. The next step shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a month 30 days long instead of 29
Adding a 13th month to make a leap year

phrases.english: Making the month full is by three.
phrases.notes: Literally 'making the month pregnant.' It means adding a 30th day to the month.

phrases.english: Making the year a leap year is by three,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of three-judge cases, now moving to calendar matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיבור החדש is by three; according to רבי מאיר, עיבור השנה is also by three.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a leap year is decided in three stages
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the discussion starts with three, is debated by five, and is finalized by seven. Still, if three finalized it, the leap year counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: They begin with three judges, they discuss it with five, and they finish with seven. But if they finished with only three, the year is a leap year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with רבי מאיר about עיבור השנה. He describes a growing panel of three, then five, then seven judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, three judges only open the question, five debate it, and seven make the final decision. But he admits that if only three finished it, the decision still stands after the fact. So the larger panel is the proper way, but not something that cancels the result.

keyTerms.meaning: They discuss and debate (literally 'they carry and give')
They finish / make the final decision
It is a leap year (the decision counts)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבן שמעון בן גמליאל cancels a decision made by three. He says seven is the right way, but if three finished it, the leap year still counts.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
With three they begin,
and with five they debate,
and they finish with seven.
And if they finished with three, it is a leap year.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מַתְחִילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר's ruling on עיבור השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיבור השנה starts with three, is debated by five, and is finalized by seven; after the fact, three is enough.

steps.title: Laying hands on elders and the heifer ritual: three or five judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says סמיכת זקנים and עריפת עגלה need three. רבי יהודה says five.
steps.simpleTranslation: The laying of hands by the elders and the breaking of the heifer's neck are done by three, says רבי שמעון. רבי יהודה says: by five.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists two ceremonies that happen in front of judges, and two תנאים disagree about how many judges are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are court ceremonies, not lawsuits. רבי שמעון puts them with the standard three-judge cases. רבי יהודה says they need a larger group of five.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders laying hands (in the משנה's context, on a communal offering)
Breaking the neck of a calf when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown

phrases.english: The laying of hands by the elders and the breaking of the calf's neck are by three,
phrases.notes: The calf ritual is in דברים 21:1-9.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.
Rabbi Yehuda says: by five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of court matters, now with court ceremonies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: סמיכת זקנים and עריפת עגלה need three; רבי יהודה: five.

steps.title: חליצה and מיאון are done before three
steps.stepSummary: חליצה and מיאון are both done in front of three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: חליצה and the refusals are done before three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two marriage-related procedures to the list of three-judge matters. No one argues here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה frees a widow from her tie to her husband's brother. מיאון is when a young girl married off by her mother or brother refuses to stay married. Both need a court of three to be done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a childless widow from יבום
Refusals: a girl under age leaving a marriage arranged by her mother or brother

phrases.english: Chalitza and the refusals are by three.
phrases.notes: The חליצה ceremony is in דברים 25:5-10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more items to the three-judge list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה and מיאונין are done before three.

steps.title: Appraising holy produce, consecrated items and movable valuations
steps.stepSummary: Valuing נטע רבעי and מעשר שני of unknown value, הקדשות, and movable ערכין is done by three. רבי יהודה says one of them must be a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fourth-year fruit and second tithe whose value is not known are valued by three. Consecrated items are valued by three. Movable property for valuation pledges is valued by three. רבי יהודה says: one of them must be a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns to setting prices: holy produce and holy property have to be valued, and three judges do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When holy produce or property is redeemed with money, someone has to decide what it is worth. The משנה says three judges set that price. רבי יהודה adds a condition: one of the three must be a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its fourth year, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed
Items dedicated to the בית המקדש
Pledges to give a set value of a person to the בית המקדש
A priest

phrases.english: Fourth-year fruit and second tithe
whose value is not known are by three.
Consecrated items are by three.
Valuations that are movable property are by three.
phrases.notes: The ערכין pledges are in ויקרא 27:1-8.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד מֵהֶן כֹּהֵן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: one of them is a priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶטַע רְבָעִי וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין דָּמָיו יְדוּעִין – בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ceremonies to appraising the value of holy items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Appraisals of נטע רבעי, מעשר שני, הקדשות and movable ערכין are by three; רבי יהודה requires one to be a כהן.

steps.title: Land and people are appraised by nine plus a priest
steps.stepSummary: Appraising consecrated land needs nine judges and a כהן, and appraising a person is done the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Land is appraised by nine and a כהן. A person is appraised the same way.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of appraisals by saying land needs a much bigger panel: nine plus a כהן. A person's value is set the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now every appraisal was done by three judges. Here the number jumps to ten (nine plus a כהן) for land. 'Like them' tells us that valuing a person follows the land rule, not the three-judge rule for movables.

keyTerms.meaning: Land, real estate
Just like them, in the same way

steps.whatToRemember: Most matters in this list are decided by three judges. Exceptions: עיבור השנה (seven, per רבן שמעון בן גמליאל), the five of רבי יהודה for the ceremonies, and land and people, which need nine plus a כהן.

phrases.english: And land is by nine and a priest.
And a person is like them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the land just mentioned. So valuing a person also needs nine and a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the three-judge appraisals by giving land and people a larger panel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrated land is appraised by nine and a כהן; a person is appraised the same way.

steps.title: Capital cases need twenty-three judges
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that דיני נפשות are judged by a court of 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: Capital cases are judged by twenty-three judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from money and appraisal cases to life-and-death cases. It says these need a court of 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the list mostly dealt with courts of 3, 5, 7, and 10 (nine plus a כהן). Twenty-three came up only in disputes, for מוציא שם רע and מכות. Now the משנה states 23 as the plain rule for every case where a life is at stake, and the next few steps apply it to animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Capital cases, where the court can sentence someone to death
Twenty-three, the size of a 'small סנהדרין'

steps.whyThisMatters: The number 23 becomes the measuring stick for the next cases. Anything treated 'like a capital case' gets 23 judges.

phrases.english: Capital cases are judged by twenty-three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 10-judge appraisals of Step 10 to a new category, capital cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דיני נפשות require a court of 23.

steps.title: Animals involved in bestiality are judged by twenty-three
steps.stepSummary: The רובע and the נרבע are judged by 23, learned from two פסוקים that tie the animal's death to the person's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal that lay with a person, and an animal that a person lay with, are judged by twenty-three, as it says 'you shall kill the woman and the animal,' and it also says 'and you shall kill the animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the 23-judge rule to an animal that is put to death for bestiality. It brings two פסוקים as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the woman and the animal in the same breath. So the animal is killed through the same kind of court process as the person, which means 23 judges. The second פסוק covers the case of a man with an animal, so both cases are included.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that actively lay with a person
An animal that a person lay with
'And it also says': brings a second פסוק

phrases.english: An animal that lay with a person, and an animal that a person lay with,
are judged by twenty-three,
as it says: 'You shall kill the woman and the animal,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:16

phrases.english: and it says: 'And you shall kill the animal.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:15. This is the case of a man with an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 23-judge rule of Step 11 to animals in bestiality cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רובע and נרבע are judged by 23, because the פסוק links the animal's death to the person's.

steps.title: An ox that killed a person is judged by twenty-three
steps.stepSummary: A שור הנסקל needs 23 judges, because the פסוק compares the ox's death to its owner's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox that is to be stoned is judged by twenty-three, as it says 'the ox shall be stoned and also its owner shall be put to death.' The way the owner dies is the way the ox dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another animal case: an ox that killed a person. It also needs 23 judges, and the משנה shows the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the ox's stoning and the owner's death side by side. The משנה reads this as a comparison: the ox's death goes through the same process as a person's death. A person's death sentence needs 23, so the ox's does too.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that is stoned for killing a person
The owners of the animal
'Just as... so too': a comparison formula

phrases.english: An ox that is stoned is judged by twenty-three,
as it says: 'The ox shall be stoned
and also its owner shall be put to death.'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:29

phrases.english: Just like the death of the owner, so is the death of the ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second animal case, parallel to Step 12, also tied to the 23-judge rule of Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שור הנסקל is judged by 23, because its death is compared to its owner's death.

steps.title: Dispute over wild animals that killed
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion says dangerous wild animals are put to death by 23. רבי אליעזר says anyone who kills them first gains a מצוה. רבי עקיבא agrees with the first opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wolf, lion, bear, leopard, cheetah, or snake is put to death by twenty-three. רבי אליעזר says whoever kills them first has earned a מצוה. רבי עקיבא says they are put to death by twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists dangerous wild animals and says they also need a court of 23. רבי אליעזר disagrees, and רבי עקיבא sides with the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion treats these animals like the ox: a court of 23 must sentence them. רבי אליעזר holds that no trial is needed, and that killing them quickly is a good deed. רבי עקיבא repeats the first opinion word for word, which shows he agrees with it against רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild predator, often translated as a cheetah or hyena
The one who acts first
He has earned it, meaning he gets credit for a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא's words are exactly the same as the first opinion. He is not adding anything new. He is simply siding with the first opinion against רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: The wolf and the lion, the bear and the leopard,
and the cheetah and the snake:
their death is by twenty-three.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Anyone who kills them first has earned a merit.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מִיתָתָן בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: Their death is by twenty-three.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר כׇּל הַקּוֹדֵם לְהוֹרְגָן זָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ox case of Step 13 to wild animals, and introduces a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the first opinion and רבי עקיבא, dangerous animals need 23 judges. רבי אליעזר says anyone may kill them right away.

steps.title: Trials that only the court of seventy-one can judge
steps.stepSummary: Only the court of 71 may judge a שבט, a נביא השקר, or a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court does not judge a tribe, a false prophet, or a כהן גדול except through a court of seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new, higher level: cases that only the great court of 71 can judge. It lists three kinds of defendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole tribe, a false prophet, and the כהן גדול are matters of great public weight. For them, even a court of 23 is not enough. Only the great סנהדרין of 71 may try them.

keyTerms.meaning: A tribe; here, a whole tribe that sinned
A false prophet
The High Priest
Seventy-one, the size of the great סנהדרין

phrases.english: They do not judge a tribe,
nor a false prophet,
nor a High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: except by a court of seventy-one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the 23-judge level (Steps 11–14) to the 71-judge level.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שבט, a נביא השקר, and a כהן גדול are judged only by the court of 71.

steps.title: National decisions that need the court of seventy-one
steps.stepSummary: Going out to a מלחמת הרשות, adding to ירושלים or the עזרות, and setting up local סנהדריות all need the court of 71.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not go out to an optional war, add to the city or the Temple courtyards, or set up local courts for the tribes, except by a court of seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists more matters for the court of 71. These are not trials but big national decisions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 71 court is not only for special trials. It also approves an optional war, any expansion of ירושלים or the עזרות, and the setup of local סנהדריות. These decisions affect the whole nation, so they need the highest court.

keyTerms.meaning: An optional war, one the Torah does not command
The courtyards of the בית המקדש
Local courts of 23 set up for the tribes
They add or extend

phrases.english: And they do not go out to an optional war

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: except by a court of seventy-one.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל הָעִיר וְעַל הָעֲזָרוֹת
phrases.english: They do not add to the city or to the courtyards
phrases.notes: 'The city' means ירושלים.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: except by a court of seventy-one.
They do not set up local courts for the tribes

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: except by a court of seventy-one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מוֹצִיאִין לְמִלְחֶמֶת הָרְשׁוּת אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of 71-only matters begun in Step 15, now with national decisions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An optional war, expanding ירושלים or the עזרות, and setting up tribal סנהדריות all need the court of 71.

steps.title: Declaring an idolatrous city needs seventy-one
steps.stepSummary: An עיר הנדחת may be declared only by the court of 71.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not declare a city an idolatrous city except by a court of seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more item to the 71 list: declaring a whole city to be an עיר הנדחת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עיר הנדחת means a whole Jewish city is destroyed for worshipping idols. Because this is so drastic and affects a whole community, only the great court of 71 may declare it.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people were led into idol worship and is destroyed by Torah law
They make, meaning here they declare

phrases.english: They do not declare an idolatrous city,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: except by a court of seventy-one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין עוֹשִׂין עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the עיר הנדחת to the list of 71-only matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the court of 71 may declare an עיר הנדחת.

steps.title: Limits on declaring an idolatrous city
steps.stepSummary: An עיר הנדחת is not declared on the border, and not three at once, but one or two may be declared.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not declare an idolatrous city on the border, and not three cities, but they may declare one or two.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds limits to the עיר הנדחת rule. It names cases where the court may not declare a city, even though the category applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two limits are given. A city on the border of ארץ ישראל is not declared an עיר הנדחת. Also, the court does not declare three cities at once, though one or two is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The border or frontier of the land
But: introduces what is allowed

steps.whatToRemember: Two levels of court were set here. 23 judges for life-and-death cases, including animals put to death (except that רבי אליעזר lets anyone kill wild animals). 71 judges for national matters: a שבט, a נביא השקר, a כהן גדול, a מלחמת הרשות, expanding ירושלים or the עזרות, tribal סנהדריות, and an עיר הנדחת. An עיר הנדחת is not declared on the border or three at once.

phrases.english: They do not declare an idolatrous city on the border,
and not three,
but they do declare one or two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין עוֹשִׂין עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת בַּסְּפָר וְלֹא שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how the עיר הנדחת rule of Step 17 is carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עיר הנדחת is not declared on the border or three at a time, but one or two may be declared.

steps.title: The two sizes of סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: The great סנהדרין has 71 judges and the small סנהדרין has 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: The great סנהדרין had seventy-one judges, and the small one had twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the basic numbers for the two kinds of courts. Everything after this will prove where these numbers come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps listed which cases need 71 and which need 23. Now the משנה states the two sizes plainly, so it can bring a source for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: The great high court of 71 judges
A smaller court of 23 judges

phrases.aramaic: סַנְהֶדְרִין גְּדוֹלָה הָיְתָה שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: The Great Sanhedrin was of seventy-one,
and the small one was of twenty-three.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַנְהֶדְרִין גְּדוֹלָה הָיְתָה שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from listing what each court judges to stating the size of each court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Great סנהדרין = 71 judges; small סנהדרין = 23 judges.

steps.title: Source for 71: seventy elders plus משה
steps.stepSummary: The 70 elders that משה was told to gather, plus משה himself, make 71.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the great court has 71? The פסוק says, 'Gather for Me seventy men of the elders of Israel,' and משה stood at their head.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks for the source of the number 71 and answers it with a פסוק about the 70 זקנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 70. The extra one comes from משה, who led the group, so the full court was 71.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
The elders of Israel
At their head, over them

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד?
phrases.english: From where do we know that the great one is of seventy-one?
As it says: "Gather for Me seventy men
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:16

phrases.english: of the elders of Israel,"
and Moshe was over them.
phrases.notes: Literally "on top of them." Adding משה to the seventy gives seventy-one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the first number stated in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That the great סנהדרין has 71 judges.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 11:16, where משה is told to gather 70 elders, with משה himself at their head.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the great court has seventy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says the great סנהדרין has 70.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: seventy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different number for the great court: 70, not 71.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the same group of 70 elders but does not add משה as an extra judge. So the dispute is only about whether משה counts toward the number.

keyTerms.meaning: Seventy

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: seventy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the count of 71 from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the great סנהדרין has 70 judges.

steps.title: Source for the small court: a judging group and a saving group make twenty
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים mention an עדה that judges and an עדה that saves, which together make 20 judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the small court has 23? The פסוק says, 'The congregation shall judge,' and 'the congregation shall save.' A congregation that judges and a congregation that saves make twenty here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins to build up the number 23. This step reaches 20, and the next steps will explain the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word עדה twice: once for judging the accused and once for saving him. That means two groups: one that leans to convict and one that leans to acquit. If each עדה is ten, together they make 20.

keyTerms.meaning: A congregation, a group
A group that judges, leaning to convict
A group that saves, leaning to acquit

steps.confusionAlert: This step only reaches 20, not 23. The משנה still has to prove that an עדה is ten, and then add the last three judges.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן לַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה?
phrases.english: And from where do we know that the small one is of twenty-three?
As it says: "The congregation shall judge,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:24

phrases.english: "and the congregation shall save."
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25

phrases.english: A congregation that judges and a congregation that saves:
here there are twenty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the great court to the second number in step 19, the small court.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 35:24–25: a judging עדה and a saving עדה.

steps.title: An עדה is ten: the מרגלים
steps.stepSummary: The 10 מרגלים who spoke badly are called an 'evil עדה', so an עדה is ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know a congregation is ten? The פסוק says, 'How long for this evil congregation?' Take out יהושע and כלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up the step before by proving that an עדה means ten people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were 12 מרגלים. יהושע and כלב were not part of the evil group, which leaves ten. Since those ten are called an עדה, an עדה is ten, and so two עדות make 20.

keyTerms.meaning: The evil congregation, meaning the bad מרגלים
Take out, leave out
The two good מרגלים

phrases.english: And from where do we know that a congregation is ten?
As it says: "How long for this evil congregation?"
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:27, said about the מרגלים.

phrases.english: Take out Yehoshua and Kalev.
phrases.notes: Twelve מרגלים minus these two leaves ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the count of 20 in step 22 by defining עדה as ten.
steps.raayaObject: That an עדה is ten people.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 14:27: the ten bad מרגלים are called an עדה.

steps.title: Where do the three extra judges come from?
steps.stepSummary: Having reached 20, the משנה asks for the source of the last three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know to add three more?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The משנה has 20 judges and now looks for a source for the remaining three, which the next steps will begin to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is 23, so three judges are missing. The answer will come from a פסוק about following the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: To add three more

phrases.english: And from where do we know to bring three more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the 20 judges established so far to the missing three.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the three judges beyond 20.

steps.title: Do not follow the majority to convict
steps.stepSummary: From 'do not follow a majority for evil,' we learn that following the majority for good, to acquit, is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what is implied by the words 'Do not follow a majority for evil,' I understand that I may go with them for good.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts its answer by reading a פסוק. It notes that the פסוק forbids following the majority to convict, which implies you may follow the majority to acquit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only rules out following the majority 'for evil', meaning to convict. That suggests following the majority 'for good', meaning to acquit, is fine. This first reading sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From the implication
For evil, meaning to convict
For good, meaning to acquit

phrases.english: From the implication of what is said:
"Do not follow a majority for evil,"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:2

phrases.english: I understand that I may be with them for good.
phrases.notes: "For evil" here means to convict; "for good" means to acquit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 24 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the majority may be followed to acquit.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק also say 'incline after a majority'?
steps.stepSummary: If following the majority to acquit is already implied, why does the פסוק add 'incline after a majority'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'incline after a majority'?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה points out a problem: the same פסוק also says to follow the majority, which seems to repeat what was already understood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 already showed that the majority may be followed to acquit. So the words 'incline after a majority' look extra. The answer in the next step will show these words teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why does it say?
To incline, to lean toward a ruling

phrases.english: If so, why does it say
"Incline after a majority"?
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, שמות 23:2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 25 by pointing to extra words in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'אחרי רבים להטות' in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following the majority to acquit is already implied, so these words seem extra.

steps.title: Acquit by a majority of one, convict by a majority of two
steps.stepSummary: The extra words teach that leaning to acquit needs a majority of one, but leaning to convict needs a majority of two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Your leaning to acquit is not like your leaning to convict. Leaning to acquit is by a majority of one; leaning to convict is by a majority of two.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question: the extra words teach that acquitting and convicting need different majorities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To acquit, winning by one vote is enough. To convict, the majority must be at least two votes. This rule is why the court needs judges beyond the 20, since it must be able to produce a majority of two.

keyTerms.meaning: Your leaning, your deciding vote direction
By a majority of one
By a majority of two

steps.whatToRemember: Acquitting needs a majority of one; convicting needs a majority of two. This comes from the extra words 'incline after a majority', and it is the base for adding judges beyond the 20.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows the Torah makes it harder to convict than to acquit. It is the key to finishing the count of 23 judges.

phrases.english: Your leaning for good is not like your leaning for evil.
Your leaning for good is by one,
phrases.notes: A majority of just one judge is enough to acquit.

phrases.english: your leaning for evil is by two.
phrases.notes: To convict, the majority must be at least two judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 by giving the extra words their own lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra words a new teaching, so they are not repetitive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'incline after a majority' just repeat that we follow the majority to acquit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words teach that convicting needs a majority of two, while acquitting needs only one.
